LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.3: Rhythm and pattern making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm and pattern making, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are rhythms created?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different sound durations in simple songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and pattern making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a simple rhythmic pattern using long and short sounds,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and pattern making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. play rhythmic accompaniments to simple songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and pattern making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. move in rhythm around basic shapes drawn on the floor,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and pattern making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. make a random repeat patterns using found objects,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Rhythm and pattern making in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.  Learners to listen to or watch live or recorded performances of simple songs and clap their rhythmic patterns. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.  Learners to take turns to recite short and long sounds in a simple rhythmic pattern using French rhythm names. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time.  Learners to play simple body percussion rhythmic accompaniments to familiar songs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  In purposive groups, learners to draw/trace/mount/stamp geometric basic shapes on the ground and move in rhythm on the shapes drawn, by skipping, sliding or galloping observing safety. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm and pattern making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Creativity and imagination: as the learner creates simple rhythmic patterns using short and long sounds.

 Self- efficacy: as the learner confidently plays rhythmic accompaniment to familiar songs.

 Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner in groups, draws geometric basic shapes on the ground and moves in

rhythm on the shapes drawn.

Values:
 Responsibility: is enhanced as the learner takes care of the digital devices as they record the rhythmic chant performances

for future use.

 Respect: is promoted as the learner gives chance to peers as they take turns to recite short and long sounds using French

rhythm names.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Life skills: are enhanced as the learner applies skills acquired to safely and rhythmically move while skipping, sliding and

galloping around basic shapes drawn on the ground.

 Social cohesion: is promoted as the learner portrays team spirit as they work with peers to recite short and long sounds

using French rhythm names.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: as the learner applies knowledge and skill gained in Mathematics to count and maintain the beat as they move in

rhythm on the shapes drawn to accompany a familiar song.

Suggested learning resources:

Relevant virtual sites, resource persons, flash cards, digital devices, pictures, reference books, audio /visual recordings of music,

assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key

guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand
